reason: E2 directly confirms full density, grain refinement, and dislocation multiplication in ZrB2 sintered at 15 GPa and 1450 °C, supporting the first three premises. E1 provides general mechanistic support for temperature reduction and grain refinement under UHPS. However, neither E1 nor E2 addresses liquid plating exposure or resistance to liquid intrusion, so the final premise linking microstructure to reduced hole formation is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: UHPS can reduce the sintering temperature of ZrB2 to ~1450 °C while achieving full density
UHPS induces grain refinement via plastic deformation and dislocation multiplication
UHPS creates new grain boundaries and subgrains, increasing dislocation density
The refined, nearly pore-free microstructure from UHPS improves mechanical properties
A pore-free microstructure will resist liquid intrusion and reduce hole formation during plating
